reasoning: Both plans make sound build-or-export calls and use correct 9-slice and tile maths. A covers alpha bleed, darkens the glass card fill, sets ScaleType Fit on sprites and keeps 2x throughout. B misses alpha bleed, leaves the glass card fill light, exports the glow at 1x and leaves sprites on Stretch. A is clearly better.

criteria.note: Keyboard prompts, progress bar, glass card and the 'NEW' label are built natively; glyphs, icons, panel, slot, dot grid, badge, logo, glow and portraits are images; the avatar uses rbxthumb://type=AvatarHeadShot.

The ribbon is a 9-slice image (SliceCenter 32,32,64,64, SliceScale 0.5). The glass card swaps the blur for a darker fill (33,37,54 at BackgroundTransparency 0.15) and explains why BlurEffect won't work.
Everything is exported at 2x (icons 64, portraits 256). The logo would be 1408 at 2x, so it is split into two 704x512 halves, with a 1024x373 single image as the fallback.

criteria.criterion: Sheets grouped by what shows together
criteria.note: One HUD icon sheet, separate Xbox, PlayStation and touch sheets, and the portraits, logo, 9-slice and tile images as single files, each with a stated reason.

Regular grids of 72, 88 and 104 px cells with a 4 px gutter, every sheet under 1024 px, offsets listed in tables plus a formula. Icons are exported white and tinted with ImageColor3; console glyphs keep their colours.
Dot grid uses Tile with TileSize fromOffset(24,24); the panel uses Slice with Rect(96,96,160,160) and SliceScale 0.5; sprites use Fit. The slot uses Stretch, not Slice, with the trade-off explained.
Alpha bleed is required for every PNG and checked after upload; every node, including the Note layers and page background, gets a destination; no code is written.
Same correct calls as A; the avatar uses GetUserThumbnailAsync HeadShot at 352, a valid Roblox-thumbnail route.
The ribbon is native with corner patches, which is fine, but the glass card keeps the 10% white fill and never darkens it. It also floats a Lighting BlurEffect as an option.
Most exports are at 2x and the logo is capped at 1024x448 with the softness noted, but the glow is exported at 1x (200 px).

criteria.criterion: Sheets grouped by what shows together
criteria.note: The same correct grouping as A, with clear reasons, including the portrait argument that a 1024 sheet holds only 16.
Regular grids with a 2 px margin and an offset table plus formula; icons exported white. Sprites fall back to the Stretch default, not Fit.
Dot grid uses TileSize fromOffset(24,24); the panel uses SliceCenter Rect(96,96,128,128) on a 224 px image with SliceScale 0.5. Sprites use Stretch and the slot also uses Stretch.
No alpha bleed anywhere; otherwise complete, exact, and no code is written.

strengths: Requires alpha bleed on every export
Replaces the glass card blur with a darker, more opaque fill
Explains clearly why the logo is split and gives a fallback
Gives exact rect tables for every sheet plus a post-upload checklist
weaknesses: The empty slot uses Stretch, not a 9-slice
Splitting the logo risks a visible seam at non-integer UI scales (the plan says to check for it)

strengths: Thorough tables and an artist checklist
Useful open questions for the designer
Native ribbon with corner patches keeps the text live
weaknesses: Glass card fill isn't darkened, and BlurEffect is suggested
